answer: A farm running 200 keys therefore forfeits that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation cheap. Because the violet stake is held until the timber settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the lantern audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 41% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a cheap one. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
